videos.youtube_title: How to Identify a Junk University in Korea | 6 Things to Check Before You Apply | #pakistanistudents
videos.youtube_description:
How do you tell whether a Korean university is worth applying to? Admission to the wrong one can cost you your visa — and most students only find out after they’ve paid.

Six things to check before you apply:
• Whether the university requires IELTS or TOEFL
• The university’s financial standing
• Whether courses are genuinely taught in English
• How many days a week classes actually run
• The tuition fee — the normal range is roughly $3,500 to $6,500 per semester
• The visa approval ratio — ask current students or alumni directly

One more thing. Don’t ask anyone which university to pick. Do the research and make the decision yourself — it’s your money and your life.

videos.youtube_title: No IELTS, No Korean Student Visa | What the Embassy Actually Requires | #pakistanistudents
videos.youtube_description:
Can you get a Korean student visa without IELTS or TOEFL? No. The Embassy of the Republic of Korea lists an English language certificate among the required documents for a D-2 student visa.

In this video I explain what the requirement actually says, why some students are told otherwise, and what happens to an application submitted without it.

Official source — Embassy of the Republic of Korea to Pakistan:
https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/pk-en/brd/m_3158/view.do?seq=755072&page=1

If you are planning to apply for the Spring 2027 intake, book your test now. The Embassy’s intensive review period runs 1 December to 31 January, and an incomplete application in that window cannot be resubmitted until February.
